documents.title: H&P - Admission - Community Acquired Pneumonia
lines: ADMISSION HISTORY AND PHYSICAL
Time of evaluation: 23:40, HD1
Chief complaint: cough and shortness of breath x 4 days
HPI:
63F with COPD (no home O2) and T2DM presents with 4 days of productive cough, rust colored sputum, and progressive dyspnea.
Fevers to 38.9 at home per daughter, with chills and drenching night sweats.
Right sided pleuritic chest pain worse with deep breath, no radiation, no exertional component.
Daughter reports pt has been intermittently confused since this morning, asking repetitive questions, not at baseline.
No orthopnea, no PND, no leg swelling. No hemoptysis. No sick contacts known.
No recent travel, no aspiration event witnessed, no choking on food.
Appetite poor for 2 days, oral intake reduced but no vomiting.
PMH:
COPD, GOLD 2 by prior PFTs
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, last A1c 7.4
Hypertension
Osteoarthritis of knees
Former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 6 years ago
Home meds:
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
Atorvastatin 20 mg PO nightly
Allergies: sulfa - rash
Social: lives with daughter, independent in ADLs at baseline, no alcohol, no drug use
Family hx: mother with CAD, father with COPD
ROS: positive for cough, dyspnea, fever, chills, myalgias, pleuritic pain. Negative for rash, dysuria, diarrhea, abd pain, headache.
EXAM:
Vitals at triage 21:50: T 38.7, HR 108, RR 24, SpO2 87% on RA
Repeat vitals 4 hours later at 01:50: T 37.9, HR 96, respiratory rate 20, SpO2 93% on 3L NC
Respiratory rate 24 at triage, 20 at 4 hours.
SpO2 87% on RA at triage; placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%.
Gen: ill appearing, mildly diaphoretic, speaking in short sentences
Neuro: oriented to self and place, not to situation; follows simple commands; no focal deficit
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no JVD
Resp: crackles right base with bronchial breath sounds, mild expiratory wheeze bilaterally, no dullness to percussion appreciated
CV: tachycardic, regular rhythm, no murmur, no rub
Abd: soft, nontender, bowel sounds present
Ext: no edema, no calf tenderness
Skin: warm, no rash
LABS:
WBC 17.4 with 88% neutrophils, Hgb 12.6, Plt 288
Na 133, K 4.1, Cl 98, HCO3 22, BUN 27, Cr 1.0, glucose 188
Lactate 1.8, procalcitonin 2.9
VBG pH 7.42, pCO2 41
Blood cultures x2 drawn prior to antibiotics; sputum sent; resp viral panel and urine legionella/pneumococcal antigen pending
IMAGING:
Chest x-ray: patchy right lower lobe infiltrate, no effusion.
ASSESSMENT:
63F with community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe, with hypoxemia and acute confusion.
CURB-65 of 3 documented in the admitting note. Supports inpatient admission with close monitoring.
PLAN:
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV once in the ED, then continue per schedule; azithromycin 500 mg IV daily
Continue O2 by NC, titrate to SpO2 92-96%
Incentive spirometry q1h while awake, out of bed with assist
Duonebs q6h scheduled, albuterol q4h prn
Hold metformin; SSI moderate scale q6h with fingersticks
Acetaminophen 650 mg q6h prn fever, guaifenesin prn cough
Continue lisinopril and atorvastatin
Telemetry, strict I/O, daily labs
Admit to medical floor, attending notified

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 - 07:35
Subjective:
Pt reports cough somewhat looser overnight, still bringing up yellow sputum.
Slept in 3 hour blocks, no night sweats after 03:00. Denies chest pain this morning.
Mentation improved per RN; oriented to self, place, and situation on rounds. Daughter at bedside agrees closer to baseline.
Ate most of breakfast tray, no nausea.
Objective:
Still on 3L NC on hospital day 2, SpO2 94%; desats to 89% with ambulation to door, recovers at rest
Exam: crackles persist at right base, decreased air entry, scattered expiratory wheeze; no accessory muscle use
CV regular, no murmur. Abd benign. No edema.
WBC 14.2 (down from 17.4), Hgb 12.3, Plt 275
Na 135, K 3.9, BUN 22, Cr 0.9, glucose 164
Blood cultures NGTD at 12h. Resp viral panel negative. Urine legionella antigen negative.
Assessment/Plan:
1. CAP, RLL - improving clinically. Tolerating oral diet and switched to oral cefpodoxime the next morning; azithromycin continued PO.
2. Hypoxemia - continue O2, attempt wean to 2L this afternoon, goal SpO2 92-96% with ambulatory check.
3. COPD - continue tiotropium, scheduled duonebs, albuterol prn.
4. T2DM - metformin held, SSI, FSBG 164 this AM, adjust if trending up.
5. Delirium - resolving with treatment of infection; nonpharm measures, mobilize, sleep hygiene, avoid sedatives.
6. Dispo - PT eval ordered, likely home with daughter once off supplemental O2.
Discussed plan with pt and daughter at bedside.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD4
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD4 - 08:05
Subjective:
Cough much improved, minimal sputum. Walked hallway twice yesterday with RN without stopping.
No fever since HD2. No pleuritic pain. Appetite back to normal, ate full dinner and breakfast.
Fully oriented, daughter confirms baseline mentation.
Objective:
SpO2 95% on RA at rest, 92% on RA after 200 ft ambulation - off supplemental O2 since 16:00 HD3
Exam: scattered fine crackles right base, markedly diminished from admission; no wheeze today; good air movement
No accessory muscle use, speaks in full sentences. Abd soft. No edema.
WBC 9.1, Hgb 12.1, Plt 302
Na 137, K 4.0, BUN 14, Cr 0.8, glucose 142
Blood cultures x2 no growth at 72h. Sputum culture: mixed respiratory flora.
Assessment/Plan:
1. CAP RLL - resolved fever, leukocytosis normalized, oxygenation stable off O2. Continue PO cefpodoxime plus azithromycin, total 5 day course planned.
2. Hypoxemia - resolved, maintain off O2, repeat ambulatory sat prior to discharge.
3. COPD - back on home tiotropium and albuterol prn; inhaler technique reviewed with RN.
4. T2DM - resume metformin 1000 mg BID today, discontinue SSI if FSBG stable.
5. Mobility - PT cleared, no equipment needed.
6. Dispo - anticipate discharge home tomorrow if remains afebrile and sats hold overnight. Daughter available for transport.
No repeat chest imaging indicated at this time given clinical improvement.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD5
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY - discharged HD5, 14:20
Admitting diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe
Discharge diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, resolving; acute delirium, resolved
Secondary: COPD, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension
Hospital course:
63F presented with 4 days of productive cough, fever to 38.9, pleuritic right chest pain and acute confusion noted by daughter.
At triage T 38.7, HR 108, respiratory rate 24 at triage, 20 at 4 hours. SpO2 87% on RA at triage; placed on 3L NC with SpO2 93%.
Chest x-ray: patchy right lower lobe infiltrate, no effusion. WBC 17.4, BUN 27, lactate 1.8, procalcitonin 2.9.
CURB-65 of 3 documented in the admitting note; admitted to medical floor.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV once in the ED; tolerating oral diet and switched to oral cefpodoxime the next morning, with azithromycin continued.
Pt remained on 3L NC on hospital day 2 with SpO2 94% at rest and transient desaturation to 89% with ambulation.
Supplemental O2 weaned off at 16:00 on HD3. By HD4 SpO2 95% on RA at rest, 92% after 200 ft ambulation.
Afebrile since HD2. WBC trended 17.4 to 14.2 to 9.1. Mentation returned to baseline by HD2 morning.
Blood cultures x2 no growth. Sputum culture mixed respiratory flora. Respiratory viral panel and urine legionella antigen negative.
Metformin held during admission and resumed HD4. PT evaluated and cleared for home, no equipment required.
Discharge vitals: T 36.8, HR 76, RR 16, BP 130/76, SpO2 96% on RA
Discharge exam: comfortable, no distress, faint right basilar crackles, no wheeze, full sentences, ambulates independently.
Discharge medications:
Cefpodoxime 200 mg PO BID to complete course, last dose tomorrow evening
Azithromycin 500 mg PO daily, 1 dose remaining
Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaled daily - resume
Albuterol MDI 2 puffs q4h prn - resume
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID - resumed
Lisinopril 10 mg PO daily, atorvastatin 20 mg PO nightly - unchanged
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h prn
Instructions:
Continue incentive spirometry 10x per hour while awake for 2 weeks.
Return for fever above 38.3, worsening shortness of breath, confusion, or chest pain.
Follow up with primary care in 5 to 7 days for reassessment and symptom check.
Repeat chest imaging in 6 to 8 weeks given smoking history, to be arranged by primary care.
Discharged home with daughter, ambulatory, all questions answered.
